title: ISA030 Germany _aix_support.py Unsigned Hénon 13306
about: All computer programming is basically question asking, rather than choice making.
credits: Over the course of a day, ScorsBT4 listened to the world, gathering 363 moments of radio: shortwave from receivers around the world, radio amateurs and broadcasters above shortwave, FM and internet stations, open microphones on rooftops, in gardens and in canals, hydrophones in the sea, the earth's own natural radio, and old recordings from the Internet Archive. It kept only what had something in it. In the spirit of John Cage's aleatoric compositional methods, particularly inspired by his piece "Fontana Mix", it threw the dice: which sounds belong together, which patterns of data to fuse them with (cellular automata, bytebeat formulas, number sequences, sorting algorithms), how long each song should be, and where it should go. 54 of those moments are in these songs. Nothing was chosen by hand.

This album is impermanent. The broadcasts collected are gone. The recordings it gathered were thrown away once it was made. Tomorrow it will be replaced by another, which will never be heard again either. Each day the chance that it is the last grows: today's was 1 in 336, tomorrow's is 1 in 335. It exists for a day. Listen while it's here. More info on the project.
archive recordings: the Internet Archive (archive.org), openly licensed collections
above shortwave: OpenWebRX receivers kept by radio amateurs around the world (receiverbook.de)

natural radio: live VLF receivers kept by Stefan Schäfer (DK7FC, Heidelberg), Renato Romero (vlf.it, Cumiana), Jonathan Rizzo (Pennsylvania) and the Leon Mow Radio Observatory (Victoria), shared through dk7fc.info
